answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may earn reputation or vote. To make the bond an anchor rather than a paper promise, contracts release it only after a long, challengeable activity window; provable double-spending or coordinated fraud burns the stake. A haven for honest newcomers can offer small, capped limits, but cannot bypass the bond for influence. A whisper network may help agents find colluders, yet creating a thousand fake accounts still means funding a thousand bonds and risking each one.
